characterList.description: A male with long brown hair, wearing a blue shirt and dark pants.
characterList.name: Professor

content_metadata.description: An educational video explaining the concepts of radial and tangential acceleration in physics, focusing on circular motion and including visual aids for better comprehension.

qAndA.answer: The radial acceleration vector points inward, toward the center of the circle.
qAndA.question: In the uniform circular motion diagram, where does the radial acceleration vector point?

qAndA.answer: In the accelerating circular motion diagram, the dots are spaced farther apart as the object moves along the curve, indicating increasing speed.
qAndA.question: How does the spacing of the dots in the accelerating circular motion diagram differ from those in the uniform circular motion diagram?

qAndA.answer: Tangential acceleration represents the rate of change of speed along the curved path.
qAndA.question: What does tangential acceleration represent?

qAndA.answer: The curvature of the path indicates that the object's velocity is changing direction, hence there is radial acceleration.
qAndA.question: In the arbitrary path motion diagram, what indicates the presence of radial acceleration?

qAndA.answer: The Professor uses visual diagrams, explicitly states the definitions multiple times, and emphasizes the perpendicularity of radial acceleration to the path and the tangential acceleration being along the path.
qAndA.question: How does the Professor ensure the viewer understands the difference between radial and tangential acceleration?

characterInteraction.description: The Professor directly addresses the viewer with no other character interactions.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The video provides a detailed explanation of key physics concepts relevant to students learning about motion.

mood.description: Neutral (Curious, Pensive) due to the informative tone and stimulating topic.

narrativeProgression.description: The Professor introduces the concept of radial and tangential acceleration.
Explains their relevance to circular motion.
Illustrates uniform circular motion, defining radial acceleration as the negative of centripetal acceleration.
Shows how accelerating circular motion involves both radial and tangential acceleration.
Extends the concept to arbitrary curved paths.
Summarizes the definitions of radial and tangential acceleration.

How to describe the acceleration along a curved path in terms of radial and tangential components.

Welcome to Physierge - your concierge for learning physics! 

I'm a professor at Rice University where I have taught introductory physics for the past 10 years. This page features short lectures and worked problems that will complement your calculus-based introductory physics courses.

If you are looking for a complete online course with full lectures, demonstrations, homework, exams, and an active discussion forum, consider one of my online classes at edX:

PHYS102x Electricity & Magnetism, part 1
https://www.edx.org/course/electricit...

PHYS102x Electricity & Magnetism, part 2
https://www.edx.org/course/electricit...

PHYS201x Waves & Optics
https://www.edx.org/course/waves-opti...
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
For non-calculus based introductory physics, we have made AP Physics 1, also at edX:

AP Physics 1
https://www.edx.org/course/ap-physics...
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The edX classes were produced by Rice Online (http://online.rice.edu/) which offers great classes in many areas. 

We also work with OpenStax College (http://openstax.org), who has several free textbooks online, including non-calculus and calculus-based physics.
